messages.subject: Bug with long file paths
messages.body_plain:
It is probably not very common (and easy to work around), but I thought I would inform you either way.  Ultimately, it seems that if the path to the BAM file is >=300 characters, then featureCounts will not open the BAM for processing.

My setup:
I have featureCounts installed inside a Debian-based Docker image.  The version is 1.6.3.  I have not tried *outside* of a Docker container-- maybe there is some problem introduced from running it inside the container?

The problem:
We use the Broad Institute's Cromwell tool with WDL-based pipelines.  Anyone who has worked with these tools knows that they use many UUIDs, and as a result, files typically have very long paths.  The exact call that caused the problem was:

featureCounts \
    -s0 \
    -t exon \
    -g gene_name \
    -a /cromwell_root/cnap-hsph-resources/grch38.95/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.95.gtf \
    -o HBR_Rep3_ERCC-Mix2_Build37-ErccTranscripts-chr22.primary.feature_counts.tsv \
    /cromwell_root/cnap-hsph-cromwell/SingleEndRnaSeqAndDgeWorkflow/01cc08e4-b897-4b39-aa37-e9d627e2b35c/call-single_sample_process/shard-3/single_sample_rnaseq.SingleSampleRnaSeqWorkflow/3ee887fb-871e-4256-9bcd-9ac7a36592c8/call-primary_filter/HBR_Rep3_ERCC-Mix2_Build37-ErccTranscripts-chr22.primary_filtered.bam

If I rename the BAM file to have a name with <300 characters, it works.  Otherwise I get:

messages.subject: Re: Bug with long file paths
messages.body_plain: There is a limit on the length of file path, which as you observed is 300 characters. We will increase this limit to a much larger value and make a new release soon. We will also issue an error message if length of file path is found to exceed the limit.

messages.subject: colorspace input ? Qual possible ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

just a quick check when dealing with old SOLiD colorspace data - it seems only -r should be used to input the .csfasta files, and the .qual files are not used (based on the answer and example command line in this forum on subjunc ). Is this true ?

It seems like subread might be a long term alternative to the commercial novoalignCS for dealing with legacy SOLiD data.

Thanks!
Colin

messages.subject: colorspace input ? Qual possible ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Colin,

You are right -- both subread-align and subjunc don't use the ".qual" files associated with the color-space sequencing data. For the base-space sequencing data, although the quality strings are written into the BAM or SAM files, our mapping algorithm doesn't take the base quality into account. The only use of the quality strings is in our exactSNP program -- low quality bases can be optionally ignored for SNP calling.

Cheers,
Yang
